speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I see you have some skin lesions; can you tell me how long they have been present and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions flat-topped and flesh-colored with a central dimple, and have they spread to other areas of the body? I also need to know if the child has had any recent fever or respiratory symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of pearly papules with central umbilication is classic for Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
